interruption.what: A session limit (the subscription's, not a spend event) killed six of the twelve first-wave readers at about 05:17 local on 2026-09-12. Nine batches had already written their complete verdict file; three (A5, B4, B5) had written nothing.
interruption.singleWriteProperty: Each reader writes its batch file in ONE Write call after its last packet is read. This is a property of the instrument, not luck: an interrupted reader leaves nothing rather than a partial file that looks complete. Evidence read from the readers' own transcripts: each surviving file came from exactly one Write call placed after the last packet-reading tool call; the three empty batches made zero Write calls; every packet id of every batch appears in that reader's Read, Grep or Bash calls before its write (130 of 130 in the first wave).
interruption.caveat: A tool call proves a packet was requested, not absorbed; the examined field in each verdict is the reader's own statement of what it read. This does not weaken the verdicts and is kept on the record.
interruption.ruling: Owner's ruling 2026-09-12: keep the nine complete batches, including the three whose readers were killed after writing; re-read the three empty batches whole with fresh readers, never resumed.

rerun.note: re-run after the 05:17 session limit; window 2 begins after the 06:00 Africa/Casablanca reset
